title: SVG Code Editor
description: Edit, validate, and pretty print SVG code in real time, right in your browser. No uploads, no signup required.
content: The SVG Code Editor is a free, browser based tool for viewing, editing, and cleaning up SVG markup without installing any design software. Whether you are fixing an icon exported from Figma or Illustrator, adjusting colors on a logo, or writing an SVG by hand, this editor gives you a live two panel workspace: your code on the left, a real time preview on the right, so every change you make is visible immediately.

What is an SVG, and why edit the code directly?

SVG, short for Scalable Vector Graphics, is an XML based image format, which means an SVG file is really just text. That is exactly why a code editor works so well for this kind of file: instead of relying on a heavy design application, you can open the raw markup, see exactly what is happening, and make precise changes by hand. This matters most when an SVG behaves unexpectedly, since design tools sometimes export bloated or malformed code with extra groups, unused attributes, or a missing viewBox. If you run into that specific problem, our SVG ViewBox Fixer is built to catch and correct it automatically.

Full control over every attribute

One of the most useful things about editing SVG as code, rather than clicking through a design tool's interface, is that you get full control over every attribute. You can adjust a single path's fill color, tighten up coordinates, remove unnecessary metadata left behind by an export process, or restructure groups, all without the overhead of opening a separate application. The format button in this editor handles basic indentation and line breaks for you, so pasted in code that arrived as one long unreadable line becomes easy to scan and edit by hand.

A built in icon library to get you started

This editor also includes a small built in icon library you can browse and drop directly into the code panel, useful as a starting point when you want a clean, simple icon to customize rather than starting from a blank canvas. Every icon in the library is original and free to use and modify. If you are building out a full set of icons for a project, our SVG Palette Extractor is a natural next step, letting you pull a consistent color palette from an existing icon or logo so new icons match your existing brand colors.

Multiple export options for every workflow

Once your SVG looks right in the preview, you have several ways to take it further. Copy code puts the raw markup on your clipboard, ready to paste into a component file or a stylesheet. Download SVG saves it as a standalone file. Download PNG rasterizes the current SVG onto a canvas and exports it as a flat image, useful for places that only accept raster formats, like a social media profile picture or an email signature. Copy Data URI base64 encodes the SVG into a single string ready to paste anywhere a URL is expected.

Built for CSS, React Native, and modern frontend workflows

The Copy Data URI button is especially handy if you are building a mobile app and want to embed a small icon without adding it as a separate asset file, since the resulting string works directly as a React Native Image component's source prop. If your end goal is using this SVG in a modern frontend codebase rather than an app, our SVG to CSS Data URI tool is built specifically around that CSS use case, and our Image to Tailwind Palette tool can turn any image, including a rendered SVG, into a ready to use Tailwind color theme.

Privacy first, every time

Because this editor runs entirely in your browser using your device's own memory, nothing you paste or upload is ever sent to a server, logged, or stored anywhere. That makes it a safe option for client work, unreleased branding, or any file you would rather not upload to a third party service. You can also verify an SVG's structure before using it in production with our SVG Viewer & Validator, which checks for malformed markup and common export issues.

Part of the Pixelquil ecosystem

This tool is part of the broader SVG & Design Tools collection on Pixelquil, alongside a growing set of Developer Utilities aimed at frontend workflows. All of them share the same principle behind this editor: fast, browser based, and privacy first, with no signup required for the core features.

faqs.answer: There is no hard limit set by the tool itself, but since everything runs in your browser's memory, extremely large SVG files may load slower depending on your device.

title: SVG Viewer & Validator
description: Preview any SVG and catch invalid markup, security risks, and rendering issues before you ship it.
content: Before an SVG goes into production, whether as a logo, an icon set, or a piece of user submitted content, it is worth checking two separate things: does it render correctly, and is it safe to embed. This tool checks both at once, rendering a live preview alongside a structured validation report, built around the actual SVG 1.1 specification published by the W3C rather than guesswork about what makes an SVG well formed.

Why SVGs break, and what well formed actually means

SVG is an XML based format, so the first requirement is that the markup is well formed XML, every tag properly closed, every attribute properly quoted, no stray characters breaking the structure. A single unclosed tag or unescaped ampersand is enough to make a parser reject the whole file. This tool runs your code through a real browser XML parser, the same kind of parser that will ultimately render or reject the file in production, so a pass here means the file will actually work, not just look plausible.

The viewBox attribute, and why so many exports miss it

Per the SVG 1.1 specification, the viewBox attribute defines the coordinate system used to scale the graphic inside its container. In practice, this is the single most common issue we see in SVGs exported from design tools: a missing or mismatched viewBox is usually why an icon looks correctly sized in one context and stretched, cropped, or tiny in another. This tool flags that specifically, rather than lumping it in as a generic warning, since it is the fix most likely to actually solve a real rendering bug. If this check fails, our SVG ViewBox Fixer can generate a correct one automatically.

SVGs can contain executable code, this checks for it

Unlike a JPG or a PNG, an SVG is a document, and the SVG specification explicitly allows a <script> element inside it, along with inline event handler attributes like onload or onclick. That means an SVG can carry executable JavaScript, a well documented cross site scripting vector when an application renders untrusted SVGs directly in the browser, for example an SVG uploaded by an end user and displayed without sanitization. This tool explicitly checks for embedded script tags and inline event handlers and flags them separately, so you know exactly why a file was marked as a concern rather than getting a vague security warning.

What this tool does not catch

Being upfront about limits matters as much as the checks themselves. This tool validates structure and flags known risky patterns, but it is not a substitute for server side sanitization if you are accepting SVGs from untrusted users at scale, a dedicated library such as DOMPurify configured for SVG is the right tool for that job. Similarly, a passing validation report confirms the file is well formed and free of the specific risks checked here, it does not guarantee visual correctness across every browser and rendering engine, since some edge cases around filters, fonts, and CSS still vary by implementation.

Runs entirely in your browser

Every check here runs client side using your browser's native XML parser, nothing you paste or upload is sent to a server, logged, or stored. That makes this a safe way to check unreleased branding, client files, or SVGs from a source you do not fully trust yet, without exposing that content to a third party service in the process of checking it.

Fixing what this tool finds

A validation report is only useful if you can act on it. If this tool flags a missing viewBox, the SVG ViewBox Fixer generates a corrected one automatically. For everything else, malformed markup, embedded scripts you want to strip, unnecessary attributes, our SVG Code Editor gives you a live code and preview panel to make the fix directly, part of the same SVG & Design Tools collection this validator belongs to.

faqs.question: What does well formed XML mean, and why does it matter for SVGs?
faqs.answer: SVG is built on XML, which requires every tag to be properly closed and every attribute properly quoted. A file that is not well formed XML will fail to parse in most browsers and design tools, so this is checked first, before any other validation.

faqs.question: Why is a missing viewBox flagged as an issue?
faqs.answer: The viewBox attribute, defined in the SVG 1.1 specification, controls how the graphic scales inside its container. Without it, an SVG often renders at a fixed size instead of scaling responsively, which is one of the most common causes of layout bugs with SVG icons and logos.

faqs.question: Can an SVG file actually contain a virus or malicious code?
faqs.answer: An SVG cannot contain a traditional virus, but it can contain executable JavaScript through a script tag or inline event handler attributes. This is a documented risk when applications render untrusted, user uploaded SVGs directly in the browser without sanitization, which is exactly what this tool checks for.

faqs.question: Does a passing report mean the SVG is completely safe?
faqs.answer: It means the checks performed by this tool passed. It is not a replacement for full server side sanitization if you accept SVG uploads from untrusted users at scale, where a dedicated sanitization library is the appropriate tool.

faqs.question: Is my SVG file uploaded to a server when I use this tool?
faqs.answer: No. Validation runs entirely in your browser using its built in XML parser. Nothing you paste or upload is sent anywhere or stored.

faqs.question: What should I do if my SVG fails validation?
faqs.answer: The detail text under each failed check explains the specific issue. For a missing viewBox, our SVG ViewBox Fixer can generate one automatically. For other issues, the SVG Code Editor lets you make direct corrections while watching a live preview.

faqs.question: Why does the tool check for inline event handlers separately from script tags?
faqs.answer: Both can execute JavaScript, but they are different mechanisms, a script tag contains a code block, while an inline event handler like onclick runs code in response to an interaction. Checking them separately makes it clear exactly what was found and where.

faqs.question: Does this tool support SVGs with embedded fonts or filters?
faqs.answer: Yes, the preview renders using your browser's native SVG engine, which supports fonts, filters, and gradients. Some visual edge cases in these areas can still vary slightly between browsers, which is a limitation of browser rendering generally, not of this tool's validation checks.

title: SVG ViewBox Fixer
description: Fix missing or broken viewBox attributes automatically, calculated from your SVG's actual rendered content.
content: A missing or incorrect viewBox is one of the most common reasons an SVG looks correct in one place and broken in another: stretched, cropped, or rendered at the wrong size. This tool detects the problem and calculates a corrected viewBox using the SVG's actual rendered geometry, via the same getBBox measurement browsers use internally, rather than guessing based on the file's width and height attributes alone.

What the viewBox attribute actually does

Per the SVG 1.1 specification, viewBox defines the coordinate system a viewer uses to map the SVG's internal content onto its rendered size, in the form min-x min-y width height. Without it, an SVG has no defined coordinate mapping to scale by, so it tends to render at a fixed pixel size instead of scaling responsively inside a container, which is the root cause behind most icon and logo scaling issues.

Why this happens so often with exported SVGs

Design tools like Figma and Illustrator sometimes export SVGs with width and height attributes but no viewBox, or with a viewBox that no longer matches the actual artwork after edits, extra padding, or a path that shifted outside the original bounds. A mismatch between a stated size and a graphic's real geometry is easy to miss visually until the SVG is dropped into a different sized container and the scaling breaks.

How this tool calculates a correct viewBox

Rather than reusing the width and height attributes, which can themselves be wrong or missing, this tool briefly renders your SVG off screen and calls the browser's native getBBox method on it, the same geometry calculation the rendering engine itself uses. That returns the actual bounding box of the visible content, paths, shapes, and all, which this tool then applies as a new viewBox, with a small padding margin so strokes sitting at the very edge are not clipped.

Runs entirely in your browser

The measurement and the fix both happen client side using your browser's own SVG rendering engine, nothing you paste or upload is sent to a server. Before applying a fix in production, our SVG Viewer & Validator is a good next step to confirm the rest of the file is well formed and free of other issues.

Fine tuning the result

A calculated viewBox reflects exactly what is currently in the file, so if you want extra breathing room around an icon, or want to intentionally crop part of the artwork, open the result in our SVG Code Editor to adjust the numbers directly while watching the live preview update.

faqs.question: Why does my SVG look different sizes in different places?
faqs.answer: This usually happens when the viewBox attribute is missing or does not match the SVG's actual dimensions, which affects how it scales in different containers.

faqs.question: How does this tool calculate the correct viewBox?
faqs.answer: It renders your SVG off screen and uses the browser's native getBBox method to measure the actual bounding box of the visible content, then applies that as the new viewBox with a small padding margin.

faqs.question: Will this tool change how my SVG looks?
faqs.answer: No, adding or correcting a viewBox changes how the SVG scales inside a container, not the artwork itself. The shapes and paths inside the file are not modified.

faqs.question: What if my SVG already has a viewBox?
faqs.answer: The status panel shows the current value. If it looks incorrect, clicking Fix viewBox recalculates it based on the SVG's actual content and replaces the existing value.

faqs.question: Is my SVG uploaded to a server?
faqs.answer: No. The measurement and fix both run entirely in your browser using its native SVG rendering engine. Nothing is uploaded or stored.

faqs.question: Why is a small padding added around the calculated viewBox?
faqs.answer: Without padding, strokes sitting exactly at the edge of the content can appear clipped. A small margin, proportional to the artwork's size, prevents that.

faqs.question: What if the tool says it cannot measure my SVG?
faqs.answer: This usually means the SVG has no visible content, or the markup is invalid. Check the file in our SVG Viewer & Validator first to confirm it is well formed.

title: SVG Palette Extractor
description: Extract every color used in an SVG, or apply one of 10 curated preset palettes directly onto your artwork.
content: This tool scans every fill, stroke, and gradient stop color inside an SVG and pulls them into a clean, deduplicated palette you can copy as hex codes, ready to drop into a design system, a Tailwind config, or a style guide. It also includes 10 curated preset palettes you can browse for inspiration, or apply directly onto your pasted SVG with one click.

Where colors actually live inside an SVG

Color in SVG markup can appear in several places: as a fill or stroke attribute directly on an element, inside an inline style attribute, or as a stop-color inside a linearGradient or radialGradient definition. This tool checks all three locations, so a palette extracted from a gradient heavy logo is just as complete as one from a simple flat icon.

10 preset palettes to browse or apply

Below the extracted colors, this tool includes 10 preset palettes covering common styles, from muted Tailwind style neutrals to vibrant sunset tones to a strict monochrome set. Click any preset swatch to copy its hex code, or click Apply to SVG to recolor your pasted artwork directly, each distinct color currently in your SVG maps to a color in the chosen palette, and the code and preview update immediately.

What is intentionally excluded

Values like none and currentColor are filtered out automatically, since they are not actual colors, and gradient or pattern references written as url(#id) are excluded too, since the palette shows resolved colors rather than references. This keeps the extracted list to genuinely useful, reusable color values.

Runs entirely in your browser

Extraction and palette application both happen client side, nothing you paste or upload is sent to a server. Once you have a palette you like, our SVG Code Editor is a natural next step for any further manual adjustments, part of the same SVG & Design Tools collection.

faqs.question: Does it work with gradients?

faqs.question: What happens when I click Apply to SVG on a preset?

faqs.question: Will applying a preset change my SVG's shapes?
faqs.answer: No, only color values are changed. The paths, shapes, and overall structure of the SVG stay exactly the same.

faqs.question: Why are some colors not detected?
faqs.answer: Colors referenced indirectly, such as through a CSS class in an external stylesheet rather than an inline attribute or style, are not detected, since this tool reads the SVG markup itself rather than computed styles from a linked stylesheet.

faqs.question: Is currentColor extracted as a color?
faqs.answer: No, currentColor is a reference to whatever color is inherited from the surrounding context, not an actual color value, so it is excluded from the extracted palette.

faqs.question: Can I use the preset palettes without uploading an SVG?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can browse and copy hex codes from any preset palette at any time, applying them to your own SVG is optional.

faqs.question: Is my SVG uploaded to a server?
faqs.answer: No, both extraction and palette application run entirely in your browser. Nothing you paste or upload is sent anywhere.

title: SVG to CSS Data URI
description: Convert SVGs into inline CSS ready data URIs, in both URL-encoded and base64 formats, with a ready-to-paste CSS snippet.
content: Inlining a small SVG directly into CSS as a data URI avoids a separate network request, which can genuinely help performance for icons and small decorative graphics used across a site. This tool handles the encoding for you, in both URL-encoded and base64 formats, and generates a ready to paste CSS snippet alongside the raw data URI.

URL-encoded versus base64, and why it matters

Base64 encoding is the more familiar option, but it typically adds around 33 percent to the encoded size compared to the original text, since base64 represents binary data using a fixed set of readable characters. URL encoding, which percent-encodes only the specific characters that are not valid inside a CSS url() value, usually produces a noticeably smaller result for SVG specifically, since SVG is already plain text. This tool defaults to URL-encoded for that reason, with base64 available as a toggle for cases where it is specifically required, such as certain legacy tooling or contexts outside CSS.

What the encoding step actually does

A raw SVG cannot be dropped into a url() value as is, since characters like double quotes, hashes, and parentheses have special meaning in CSS and need to be escaped or replaced. This tool swaps double quotes for single quotes, collapses unnecessary whitespace between tags, and percent-encodes the remaining reserved characters, following the same URL-encoding approach commonly recommended for inlining SVG in CSS.

When inlining makes sense, and when it does not

Inlining works best for small, frequently reused icons where avoiding a network request outweighs the benefit of the browser caching a separate file. For a large, complex illustration, or an SVG used identically across many separate pages, a regular linked file is often the better choice, since the browser only needs to download and cache it once. The size comparison shown below the output helps you judge whether a given SVG is a good candidate for inlining.

Runs entirely in your browser

All encoding happens client side, nothing you paste or upload is sent to a server. If you need this same SVG encoded specifically for a React Native Image component instead of CSS, our SVG Code Editor also includes a Copy Data URI option built around that use case, part of the same Developer Utilities collection this tool belongs to.

faqs.question: When should I inline an SVG instead of linking to a file?
faqs.answer: Inlining works well for small, frequently used icons where saving a network request matters more than browser caching the file separately. For larger or reused illustrations, a linked file is usually better.

faqs.question: Should I use URL-encoded or base64?
faqs.answer: URL-encoded is recommended for CSS use, since it typically produces a smaller result for SVG, which is already plain text. Base64 is mainly useful when a specific tool or platform requires that format.

faqs.question: Why does the tool replace double quotes with single quotes?
faqs.answer: A CSS url() value is often wrapped in double quotes, so any double quotes inside the SVG markup itself need to be changed to single quotes to avoid breaking the CSS syntax.

faqs.question: Does inlining an SVG affect how it can be styled with CSS?
faqs.answer: An SVG inlined as a background image through a data URI cannot have its individual internal elements targeted with CSS, since it is treated as a single image, not part of the DOM. For SVGs that need dynamic styling, inlining the raw SVG markup directly in HTML is a better approach.

faqs.question: Is there a size limit for the data URI?
faqs.answer: There is no limit enforced by this tool, but very large encoded strings can make stylesheets harder to read and maintain, which is part of why inlining is best suited to small, simple graphics.

faqs.question: Is my SVG uploaded to a server when I use this tool?
faqs.answer: No, all encoding happens entirely in your browser. Nothing you paste or upload is sent anywhere or stored.

faqs.question: Can I use this same output outside of CSS?
faqs.answer: The base64 format works in most contexts that accept a data URI, including an HTML img tag's src attribute. For a React Native specific workflow, our SVG Code Editor's Copy Data URI feature is built around that exact use case.

title: Image to Tailwind Palette
description: Turn any image into a full Tailwind v4 color theme, with a complete 50 to 950 shade scale generated for each dominant color.
content: Upload any image, a logo, a screenshot, a photo, and this tool identifies its dominant colors by sampling pixel data directly in your browser, then generates a full Tailwind style shade scale for each one, from 50 through 950. The result is output as a ready to paste Tailwind v4 @theme block, matching the same syntax Tailwind v4 itself uses for custom color tokens.

How dominant colors are identified

The image is drawn onto an off screen canvas, then sampled pixel by pixel. Each pixel's color is quantized, rounded to the nearest value in a reduced color space, so visually similar shades are grouped together instead of being counted as dozens of near-identical colors. The most frequent groups become your palette, with near-white and near-black buckets deprioritized, since large plain backgrounds are common but rarely the color you actually want as a theme token.

How the full shade scale is generated

Rather than giving you one flat color per swatch, each dominant color is expanded into an 11 step scale, 50 through 950, by converting it to HSL and adjusting lightness at each step while keeping the underlying hue consistent, with a small saturation taper at the lightest and darkest ends. This mirrors how Tailwind's own default palettes are structured, so the generated tokens slot naturally into places that expect a full scale, hover states, borders, backgrounds, and text, rather than a single fixed color.

Naming and using the output

Each extracted color starts with a generic name, editable directly in the tool, so you can rename it to something meaningful, like brand or accent, before copying. The generated snippet uses Tailwind v4's @theme syntax with --color-name-step custom properties, the same pattern used to define custom color scales in a real Tailwind v4 project, ready to paste into your global stylesheet.

A note on accuracy

Generated shade scales are a close, usable approximation, not a perceptual color science model. For a base color with unusual saturation, a couple of steps in the scale may read slightly differently than a hand tuned Tailwind palette would. Treat the output as a strong starting point, and adjust individual steps afterward if a specific shade needs fine tuning for accessibility contrast or brand precision.

Runs entirely in your browser

Extraction and scale generation both happen client side using the canvas API, your image is never uploaded to a server. If your source is already an SVG rather than a raster image, our SVG Palette Extractor reads exact color values directly from the markup instead of sampling pixels, part of the same SVG & Design Tools and Developer Utilities collections this tool belongs to.

title: SVG Optimizer & Minifier
description: Strip unnecessary metadata and shrink SVG file size automatically, ready for production use.
content: An SVG exported from a design tool often carries extra weight it does not need in production: editor metadata, unused IDs, redundant groups, and verbose path data. This tool strips that overhead automatically, reducing file size without changing how the SVG looks, distinct from manual editing since the process is fully automated and repeatable across many files.

faqs.question: Will optimizing change how my SVG looks?
faqs.answer: No, optimization removes unnecessary code, not visible content. The rendered result stays the same.

faqs.question: How is this different from the SVG Code Editor?
faqs.answer: The Code Editor is for manual, hands-on changes. This tool is automated cleanup focused purely on reducing file size for production.

title: Image to SVG Converter
description: Trace a raster image into editable vector SVG paths, right in your browser.
content: This tool traces a raster image, a PNG, JPG, or scanned sketch, into vector paths, converting flat pixels into an editable SVG. This is genuinely useful for turning a photographed logo, a hand drawn sketch, or a low resolution image into a scalable, editable vector, a fundamentally different process from any color, code, or size tool in this collection, since it generates new path geometry rather than working with existing SVG markup.

faqs.question: What kind of images work best for vectorization?
faqs.answer: High contrast images with clear, distinct shapes trace most accurately, such as logos and line art. Complex photographs with soft gradients are harder to trace cleanly.

faqs.question: Will the traced SVG need cleanup afterward?
faqs.answer: Often yes, especially for detailed images. The SVG Code Editor is a good next step to refine the traced result.

title: SVG to PNG Batch Converter
description: Convert multiple SVG files to PNG at once, with custom size presets.
content: Exporting a whole icon set or illustration library to PNG one file at a time is slow. This tool converts many SVG files to PNG in a single batch, with size presets so every export comes out consistently sized, a bulk workflow tool distinct from the SVG Code Editor's single file PNG export, built for people exporting entire sets rather than one icon at a time.

faqs.question: How many files can I convert at once?
faqs.answer: There is no hard limit set by the tool itself, though very large batches depend on your device's available memory since processing happens entirely in your browser.

faqs.question: Can each file use a different export size?
faqs.answer: You can apply one size preset across the batch, or export at each SVG's own native dimensions.

title: SVG Sprite Sheet Generator
description: Combine multiple SVG icons into a single sprite sheet using symbol and use references.
content: Serving many small icons as separate files means many separate network requests. This tool combines multiple SVG icons into a single sprite sheet using the standard symbol and use technique, so a page can reference any icon from one shared file. This is a specific, well established performance pattern, distinct from the CSS data URI approach, which is better suited to a small number of icons rather than a full icon library.

faqs.question: How is a sprite sheet different from inlining icons as data URIs?
faqs.answer: A sprite sheet loads once and is reused across many icon references, better suited to larger icon libraries. Data URIs work well for a small number of individually used icons.

faqs.question: Do I need JavaScript to use the generated sprite sheet?
faqs.answer: No, sprite sheets work with plain HTML using an SVG use element referencing the sheet, no JavaScript required.

title: SVG to React & Vue Component Converter
description: Convert raw SVG markup into a ready to paste React or Vue component.
content: Pasting raw SVG markup into a React or Vue project usually needs manual adjustment: converting attributes like class to className, adding props for size and color, and wrapping it as a proper component. This tool automates that conversion, producing a ready to use component file, a distinct output format from anything else in this collection, since the result is framework specific code rather than plain SVG or CSS.

faqs.question: Which frameworks are supported?
faqs.answer: React and Vue are supported, each with syntax matching that framework's conventions for attributes and props.

faqs.question: Can the generated component accept a custom color?
faqs.answer: Yes, the tool can generate a component with a color prop wired to the SVG's fill or stroke, so it can be styled dynamically.

title: SVG Path Visualizer & Point Editor
description: See and drag a path's control points visually instead of editing raw path data by hand.
content: Editing an SVG path's raw d attribute by hand means reading long strings of coordinate numbers. This tool renders a path's individual anchor points and curve handles visually, so points can be dragged directly, a fundamentally different interaction model from the code based SVG Code Editor, useful specifically for fine tuning curve shapes without decoding path syntax by eye.

faqs.question: Does this replace the SVG Code Editor?
faqs.answer: No, they serve different purposes. This tool is for visual, point by point curve adjustments. The Code Editor is better for broader structural changes.

faqs.question: Can I export the edited path back to code?
faqs.answer: Yes, dragging points updates the underlying path data, which you can then copy as standard SVG markup.

title: Favicon & App Icon Generator
description: Generate a complete favicon set and web manifest from one SVG or image.
content: A complete favicon setup needs more than one file: multiple PNG sizes, an ICO file, and often a web manifest for mobile home screen icons. This tool takes a single SVG or image and generates the full set automatically, a specific packaging task distinct from any single format converter, since it produces a complete, ready to deploy icon bundle rather than one output file.

faqs.question: What files does the generator produce?
faqs.answer: A set of PNG icons at standard sizes, an ICO file for legacy browser support, and a web manifest file for mobile and PWA icon support.

faqs.question: Can I start from a raster image instead of an SVG?
faqs.answer: Yes, both SVG and standard image formats work as a source, though starting from an SVG generally produces sharper results at every size.

title: Text to SVG Path Converter
description: Convert text into vector path outlines that render identically everywhere, no fonts required.
content: Text rendered with a font tag depends on that font being available wherever the SVG is displayed. This tool converts text into actual vector path outlines using a chosen web font, so the result renders identically everywhere without depending on font availability, a specific need for logos, wordmarks, and any text that must look pixel perfect and consistent across every environment.

faqs.question: Why convert text to paths instead of just using a font tag?
faqs.answer: Path outlines render identically regardless of whether a viewer's system has the original font installed, which matters for logos and brand consistent text.

faqs.question: Can the resulting text still be edited afterward?
faqs.answer: Once converted to paths, the content is no longer editable as text, only as vector shapes, similar to how a logo behaves after being finalized.

title: Batch SVG Color Replacer
description: Find and replace a specific color across multiple SVG files at once.
content: Rebranding an entire icon set one file at a time is tedious. This tool finds and replaces a specific color across many uploaded SVG files in a single batch operation, distinct from the Palette Extractor's single file color reading and application, since this is built specifically for bulk, multi-file color updates.

faqs.question: How is this different from the Palette Extractor's Apply to SVG feature?
faqs.answer: The Palette Extractor works on one SVG at a time. This tool is built for updating the same color across many files in one pass.

faqs.question: Can I replace more than one color at a time?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can set up multiple find and replace color pairs to apply across the batch in a single run.

title: Stroke to Fill Path Converter
description: Convert a stroked line into an equivalent filled shape for reliable scaling.
content: A stroked line's visible width can distort unpredictably when an SVG is scaled or transformed in certain contexts. This tool converts a stroke into an equivalent filled shape representing the same visible outline, so the icon scales reliably as pure fill geometry, a specific production concern for icon sets that need to behave consistently at any size.

faqs.question: Why would I need to convert a stroke to a fill?
faqs.answer: Filled shapes scale more predictably than strokes in some rendering and animation contexts, where stroke width can behave inconsistently across transformations.

faqs.question: Does this change how the icon looks visually?
faqs.answer: No, the goal is a visually identical result, just represented as fill geometry instead of a stroked line.

title: SVG Gradient Generator
description: Visually build linear and radial gradients and get the resulting SVG markup.
content: Writing gradient markup by hand, stop colors, offsets, and angles, is fiddly to get right. This tool provides a visual editor for building linear and radial gradients, drag color stops and adjust the angle directly, then copy the resulting linearGradient or radialGradient markup, a creation tool distinct from anything color related already in this collection, which focus on extracting or applying existing solid colors rather than building new gradients.

faqs.question: Does this support both linear and radial gradients?
faqs.answer: Yes, both gradient types are supported, with a visual editor for stop colors, positions, and angle or radius.

faqs.question: Can I add more than two color stops?
faqs.answer: Yes, any number of color stops can be added and positioned along the gradient.

title: Seamless SVG Pattern Generator
description: Generate tileable background patterns, dots, stripes, and grids, as SVG.
iconPath: M4 4h4v4H4z M12 4h4v4h-4z M20 4h4v4h-4z M4 12h4v4H4z M12 12h4v4h-4z M4 20h4v4H4z
content: Decorative repeating backgrounds, dots, stripes, grids, and similar patterns are commonly needed but tedious to build from scratch. This tool generates tileable SVG patterns with adjustable spacing, size, and color, a decorative background generator, a different category entirely from the icon and logo focused tools elsewhere in this collection.

faqs.question: What pattern types are available?
faqs.answer: Common options include dots, stripes, grids, and checkerboards, each with adjustable spacing and color.

faqs.question: Will the pattern tile seamlessly with no visible seams?
faqs.answer: Yes, each generated pattern is built to repeat edge to edge without visible seams when tiled.

title: Organic Blob Shape Generator
description: Generate randomized smooth, organic blob shapes for modern hero sections and backgrounds.
content: Smooth, organic blob shapes have become a common design element in modern hero sections and backgrounds, but hand drawing one that looks natural takes practice. This tool generates randomized organic blob shapes as SVG paths, with a regenerate option to explore variations, a distinct decorative shape generator rather than an icon or utility tool.

faqs.question: Can I control how irregular the blob looks?
faqs.answer: Yes, a smoothness or randomness setting adjusts how subtle or pronounced the organic irregularity is.

faqs.question: Can I change the blob's color after generating it?
faqs.answer: Yes, the generated shape is plain SVG markup with an editable fill color.

title: CSS Clip-Path Generator
description: Visually build a polygon shape and get the matching CSS clip-path value.
content: Writing a CSS clip-path polygon value by guessing coordinates is slow and error prone. This tool provides a visual editor, drag points on a shape directly over a preview, and generates the matching clip-path CSS value automatically, a CSS specific tool adjacent to SVG conceptually but distinct in output format and use case from anything else in this collection.

faqs.question: Is clip-path the same thing as an SVG clip path?
faqs.answer: They are related concepts, but this tool specifically generates a CSS clip-path property value for use directly in a stylesheet, not SVG markup.

faqs.question: Can I preview the clip-path applied to an actual image?
faqs.answer: Yes, the editor shows a live preview of the clip-path applied over a sample image as you adjust points.

title: SVG Accessibility Checker
description: Check an SVG for title and desc elements, ARIA roles, and color contrast issues.
content: An SVG that is structurally valid is not necessarily accessible. This tool checks specifically for accessibility concerns: whether a title or desc element is present for screen readers, whether appropriate ARIA roles are set, and whether foreground and background colors meet contrast guidelines, a distinct focus from the SVG Viewer & Validator, which checks structural validity and security rather than accessibility.

faqs.question: How is this different from the SVG Viewer & Validator?
faqs.answer: The Viewer & Validator checks whether an SVG is structurally valid and free of security risks. This tool checks specifically for accessibility concerns, like missing screen reader text and contrast issues.

faqs.question: What accessibility standard does the contrast check follow?
faqs.answer: Contrast checks follow WCAG color contrast guidelines, the widely used web accessibility standard for readable color combinations.

title: JSON Formatter That Shows the Exact Broken Line
description: Format and validate JSON with error line highlighting, no upload, nothing leaves your device.
content: Minified or malformed JSON is hard to debug when you cannot tell exactly where it broke. This tool formats JSON into readable, indented output, and when the input is invalid, it points to the exact line and character where parsing failed, instead of just saying invalid JSON. Useful for debugging API responses, config files, or any pasted JSON that will not parse.

faqs.question: Does this validate JSON as well as format it?
faqs.answer: Yes, invalid JSON is flagged with the specific line and character where the syntax error occurs, not just a generic error message.

faqs.question: Is my JSON data uploaded anywhere?
faqs.answer: No, formatting and validation both happen entirely in your browser. Nothing you paste is sent to a server.

title: JWT Decoder, Runs Locally in Your Browser
description: Decode a JWT's header and payload claims instantly, entirely client-side, safe for real tokens.
content: A JSON Web Token's header and payload are base64url encoded but not encrypted, so decoding them is useful for inspecting claims while debugging authentication or session issues. This tool decodes both segments instantly and displays them as readable JSON. Because it runs entirely client-side with no server round trip, it is safe to paste tokens containing real session data while debugging.

faqs.question: Does this verify the token's signature?
faqs.answer: No, this tool decodes the header and payload only. Signature verification requires the token's secret or public key, which is a separate, server-side concern.

faqs.question: Is it safe to paste a real production token here?
faqs.answer: Decoding happens entirely in your browser, nothing is sent to a server, which makes it reasonably safe for debugging. As general practice, avoid pasting sensitive tokens into any third-party tool when possible.

title: Regex Tester With Live Group Highlighting
description: Test regular expressions against sample text with live match and capture group highlighting.
content: Regular expression syntax is notoriously easy to get subtly wrong. This tool matches a regex pattern against sample text in real time, highlighting full matches and individual capture groups as you type, so you can see immediately whether a pattern behaves the way you expect before dropping it into production code.

faqs.question: Which regex flavor does this use?
faqs.answer: This tool uses JavaScript's native regular expression engine, matching the syntax and behavior you would get in a browser or Node.js environment.

faqs.question: Can I see individual capture groups, not just the full match?
faqs.answer: Yes, each capture group in your pattern is highlighted separately and listed alongside the full match.

title: UUID v4 & v7 Generator, Bulk Output
description: Generate classic random UUIDs or newer sortable UUIDv7s, in bulk, copy or export instantly.
content: UUIDs are used everywhere as unique identifiers, but not all UUID versions behave the same. This tool generates both v4, fully random, and the newer v7, which embeds a timestamp so generated IDs sort chronologically, a meaningful difference for anyone using UUIDs as database primary keys. Generate a single ID or a bulk batch, and copy or export the result.

faqs.question: What is the difference between UUID v4 and v7?
faqs.answer: v4 is fully random with no inherent order. v7 embeds a timestamp, so generated IDs sort chronologically, which can improve database index performance when used as a primary key.

faqs.question: How many UUIDs can I generate at once?
faqs.answer: You can generate a large batch in one go, generation happens instantly in your browser with no server round trip.

title: MD5, SHA-1 & SHA-256 Hash Generator
description: Generate MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, and SHA-512 hashes from text or a file, all at once.
content: This tool generates cryptographic hash digests, MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, and SHA-512, from either pasted text or an uploaded file, all calculated at once rather than one algorithm at a time. Useful for verifying file integrity, checking a checksum against a published value, or generating hashes for non-security use cases like cache keys.

faqs.question: Is MD5 secure for password hashing?
faqs.answer: No, MD5 is considered cryptographically broken for security purposes like password storage. It remains useful for basic checksums and non-security integrity checks, not for protecting sensitive data.

faqs.question: Can I hash a file instead of text?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can upload a file directly and the tool computes hashes from its contents, entirely in your browser.

title: Cron Expression Translator & Visual Builder
description: Translate a cron expression into plain English, or build one visually with a schedule picker.
content: Cron syntax is compact but easy to misread, is that field the hour or the day of month. This tool translates any cron expression into a plain English description of its schedule, and also works in reverse, letting you build a valid expression visually by picking days, hours, and intervals rather than writing the syntax from memory.

faqs.question: Does this support standard 5-field cron syntax?
faqs.answer: Yes, standard 5-field cron expressions are supported, along with common extensions like step values and ranges.

faqs.question: Can I build an expression without knowing cron syntax at all?
faqs.answer: Yes, the visual builder lets you pick a schedule using plain controls, and generates the correct cron expression for you.

title: Text & Code Diff Checker, Side-by-Side View
description: Compare two blocks of text or code and see every addition, deletion, and change highlighted.
content: Comparing two versions of a config file, an API response, or a code snippet by eye is slow and error prone. This tool shows two blocks of text side by side, with every added, removed, and changed line clearly highlighted, useful anywhere you need to spot differences quickly without relying on a full version control setup.

faqs.question: Does this work for code, not just plain text?
faqs.answer: Yes, the diff comparison works on any text input, including source code, configuration files, and structured data like JSON or YAML.

faqs.question: Is my pasted content uploaded anywhere?
faqs.answer: No, the comparison runs entirely in your browser. Neither block of text is sent to a server.

title: Live Markdown Previewer, No File Saved
description: Type markdown and see the rendered output update live, nothing saved or uploaded.
content: Markdown is simple, but knowing exactly how a README or documentation page will render before committing it saves back and forth guessing. This tool renders markdown live in a split view as you type, standard formatting, headers, lists, code blocks, and links all render exactly as they would on GitHub or a documentation site.

faqs.question: Does this support GitHub-flavored markdown, like tables and task lists?
faqs.answer: Yes, common GitHub-flavored markdown extensions including tables, task lists, and fenced code blocks with syntax highlighting are supported.

faqs.question: Is my markdown content saved anywhere?
faqs.answer: No, nothing is saved or uploaded. The preview updates live in your browser only, and clears when you leave the page.

title: HEX, RGB, HSL & OKLCH Color Converter
description: Convert instantly between HEX, RGB, HSL, and the newer OKLCH color format.
content: Modern CSS increasingly supports color formats beyond the familiar HEX and RGB, including OKLCH, a perceptually uniform color space gaining adoption for its more predictable lightness and saturation adjustments. This tool converts instantly between HEX, RGB, HSL, and OKLCH, useful when a design system or CSS codebase mixes formats or is migrating to newer color functions.

faqs.question: What is OKLCH and why would I use it?
faqs.answer: OKLCH is a color format designed to be perceptually uniform, meaning equal changes in its lightness value look equally different to the human eye, which makes building consistent color scales more predictable than with HSL.

faqs.question: Does browser support matter for using OKLCH in CSS?
faqs.answer: OKLCH is supported in all modern browsers, though it is worth checking your specific browser support requirements before relying on it as your only color format in production CSS.

title: Unix Timestamp Converter With Timezone Support
description: Convert epoch timestamps to human-readable dates across any timezone, both directions.
content: Logs, databases, and APIs frequently store dates as Unix timestamps, seconds or milliseconds since January 1, 1970, which are not human readable on their own. This tool converts a timestamp to a readable date in any timezone, and works in reverse too, turning a chosen date and time into its corresponding timestamp.

faqs.question: Does this handle both seconds and milliseconds timestamps?
faqs.answer: Yes, the tool automatically detects whether an entered timestamp is in seconds or milliseconds based on its length, and converts accordingly.

faqs.question: Can I convert a date to a timestamp in a specific timezone?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can select any timezone when converting a date to a timestamp, or when converting a timestamp to a readable date.

title: Placeholder Text Generator by Word Count
description: Generate lorem ipsum or plain-English placeholder text by exact word, sentence, or paragraph count.
content: Placeholder text fills a layout before real content is ready, and having control over exactly how much you get matters when testing how a design handles different content lengths. This tool generates text by an exact word, sentence, or paragraph count, in either classic Latin lorem ipsum or a plain-English style for a more realistic preview.

faqs.question: Can I generate placeholder text that isn't Latin lorem ipsum?
faqs.answer: Yes, a plain-English placeholder mode is available alongside the classic Latin style, useful when you want a more realistic sense of how real content will read.

faqs.question: Can I set an exact word count instead of paragraphs?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can generate text by exact word count, sentence count, or paragraph count, depending on what you need to test.

title: QR Code Generator With SVG Download
description: Generate a QR code from any URL or text and download it as clean, scalable SVG or PNG.
content: Most free QR code generators only offer a PNG export, which looks blurry when printed large or scaled up. This tool generates a QR code from any URL or text and lets you download it as either SVG, fully scalable with no quality loss, or PNG. Codes are generated fresh each time with no expiration and no tracking.

faqs.question: Why would I want an SVG QR code instead of PNG?
faqs.answer: An SVG QR code scales to any size, print materials, large signage, without losing sharpness, since it is vector-based rather than a fixed grid of pixels like PNG.

faqs.question: Do the generated QR codes expire or get tracked?
faqs.answer: No, each QR code is generated directly from your input with no tracking, no expiration, and no account required.

title: camelCase, snake_case & kebab-case Converter
description: Convert text between camelCase, snake_case, kebab-case, and PascalCase instantly.
content: Renaming a variable or converting a data field between naming conventions used by different languages or systems is a small but frequent task. This tool converts text instantly between camelCase, snake_case, kebab-case, and PascalCase, a quick copy paste utility for anyone moving code or data between conventions.

faqs.question: Which naming conventions are supported?
faqs.answer: camelCase, snake_case, kebab-case, and PascalCase are all supported, converting instantly between any of them.

faqs.question: Can I convert a whole list of names at once?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can paste multiple lines at once and each one is converted independently.

title: YAML to JSON Converter, Both Directions
description: Convert YAML to JSON or JSON to YAML instantly, with syntax errors flagged clearly.
content: YAML's whitespace sensitivity makes manual conversion to or from JSON error prone, a single misplaced indent can silently change the structure. This tool converts YAML to JSON or JSON to YAML instantly in either direction, with syntax errors flagged clearly, useful for anyone working with Docker Compose files, CI configs, or Kubernetes manifests alongside JSON-based tooling.

faqs.question: Does this preserve comments when converting YAML to JSON?
faqs.answer: No, JSON has no concept of comments, so any comments in the source YAML are not carried over in the converted output. This is a limitation of the JSON format itself, not the tool.

faqs.question: What happens if my YAML has a syntax error?
faqs.answer: The tool flags the syntax error clearly rather than producing an incorrect or silently wrong conversion.

title: Password & Memorable Passphrase Generator
description: Generate secure random passwords or memorable multi-word passphrases, fully client-side.
content: A strong password does not have to be unmemorable. This tool generates both traditional random character passwords with configurable length and character sets, and memorable multi-word passphrases built from a word list, a format that is often easier to type and recall while still being resistant to guessing. Everything is generated using your browser's cryptographically secure random number source, and nothing generated is ever sent or stored anywhere.

faqs.question: Is a passphrase as secure as a random password?
faqs.answer: A sufficiently long passphrase, several random words combined, can be comparably strong to a random character password, while being easier to remember and type.

faqs.question: Are generated passwords stored anywhere?
faqs.answer: No, generation happens entirely in your browser using a cryptographically secure random source, and nothing generated is transmitted or stored.

title: Robots.txt Tester, Check Any URL Against Any Bot
description: Test whether a specific URL is allowed or blocked for any crawler, directly against your robots.txt rules.
content: A robots.txt file can quietly block pages you never meant to hide, or allow crawlers you meant to restrict. This tool tests a specific URL against a robots.txt file's rules for any named crawler, showing clearly whether that URL is allowed or disallowed, useful for catching a misconfigured rule before it costs you indexing.

faqs.question: Can I test rules for a specific bot, not just any crawler?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can test a URL against rules for a specific named user-agent, since robots.txt rules can differ between crawlers.

faqs.question: Do I need to paste my robots.txt, or can it fetch mine automatically?
faqs.answer: You can paste rules directly, or fetch and test against a live robots.txt file by domain.

title: AI Crawler Access Checker (GPTBot, ClaudeBot & More)
description: See at a glance whether GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, and Google-Extended are allowed or blocked on your site.
content: AI crawlers like GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, and Google-Extended each respect robots.txt independently, and a site can easily end up blocking one without meaning to, or without realizing a rule change affected it. This tool checks a robots.txt file against each of these crawlers individually and reports allowed or blocked status for each one, useful for anyone deciding whether to allow AI systems to access their content.

faqs.question: Which AI crawlers does this check?
faqs.answer: GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, and Google-Extended are checked individually, since each respects robots.txt rules independently.

faqs.question: Should I allow or block AI crawlers?
faqs.answer: This is a judgment call based on your own goals around content visibility and AI systems. This tool reports current access status rather than recommending a policy.

title: XML Sitemap Generator From a URL List
description: Paste a list of URLs and get a valid XML sitemap file instantly, no crawling required.
content: Generating a sitemap usually means running a full site crawl, overkill when you already know exactly which URLs you want included. This tool takes a pasted list of URLs and generates a valid XML sitemap instantly, with optional last modified dates and priority values, ready to download or copy directly.

faqs.question: Do I need to crawl my site to use this?
faqs.answer: No, you provide the URL list directly, which is faster for smaller sites or when you already know exactly which pages should be included.

faqs.question: Can I set priority and last modified values?
faqs.answer: Yes, both are optional fields you can set per URL, or leave out entirely for a simpler sitemap.

title: XML Sitemap Validator, Catch Errors Before Submitting
description: Check an existing sitemap for structural errors and invalid URLs before submitting it to Search Console.
content: A malformed sitemap can be silently ignored or partially processed by search engines, without a clear error surfaced to you. This tool checks an existing XML sitemap for structural problems, invalid URLs, and formatting issues, so you can catch and fix them before submitting the file to Search Console.

faqs.question: What kind of errors does this catch?
faqs.answer: Structural XML errors, invalid or malformed URLs, and common formatting issues that can cause a sitemap to be rejected or partially ignored.

faqs.question: Can I validate a sitemap index file too?
faqs.answer: Yes, sitemap index files referencing multiple sitemaps are supported alongside standard single sitemap files.

title: Google SERP Snippet Preview & Pixel Length Checker
description: See exactly how a title and meta description will look in Google results, with real pixel-width truncation warnings.
content: Character count limits are a rough guide at best, since Google truncates titles and descriptions based on pixel width, not character count, and different letters take up different amounts of space. This tool renders a live preview of how a title and description will actually look in search results, with a true pixel-width warning rather than a generic character counter.

faqs.question: Why does pixel width matter more than character count?
faqs.answer: Google truncates snippets based on rendered pixel width, and letters vary in width, so two titles with the same character count can truncate differently depending on which letters they contain.

faqs.question: Does this show both desktop and mobile previews?
faqs.answer: Yes, since Google's snippet display width differs between desktop and mobile search results.

title: Open Graph Tags Generator With Live Preview
description: Generate Open Graph meta tags and preview exactly how the share card looks before publishing.
content: Open Graph tags control how a page looks when shared on Facebook, LinkedIn, and other platforms that read them, but there is no way to preview the result without actually publishing and sharing the link. This tool generates the correct og tags from your inputs and renders a live preview of the resulting share card before you ship anything.

faqs.question: Which platforms use Open Graph tags?
faqs.answer: Facebook, LinkedIn, and many other platforms and messaging apps read Open Graph tags to build link preview cards.

faqs.question: Can I preview different image dimensions?
faqs.answer: Yes, the preview reflects your specified og:image, and the tool notes the recommended dimensions for a properly cropped card.

title: Twitter/X Card Preview & Validator
description: Preview and validate a Twitter/X card without needing a live URL or an X developer account.
content: X's own card validator requires a developer account and a live, publicly accessible URL, which is not always convenient during development. This tool previews a Twitter/X card from manually entered meta tag values, and checks for common validation issues, without needing either a live URL or platform account access.

faqs.question: Do I need a live URL to use this?
faqs.answer: No, you can enter your meta tag values directly and preview the resulting card without a publicly accessible URL.

faqs.question: What card types are supported?
faqs.answer: Summary and summary_large_image card types are both supported, covering the most commonly used Twitter/X card formats.

title: JSON-LD Schema Generator for Articles & Products
description: Build valid JSON-LD structured data for common schema types through a simple form, no manual JSON writing.
content: Writing JSON-LD structured data by hand means tracking exact property names and nesting rules for each schema type. This tool generates valid JSON-LD for common types, Article, Product, FAQ, and more, through a straightforward form, so the correct structure and property names are handled for you.

faqs.question: Which schema types are supported?
faqs.answer: Common types including Article, Product, FAQPage, Organization, and Breadcrumb, covering the schema types most sites actually need.

faqs.question: Does the generated markup follow schema.org exactly?
faqs.answer: Yes, generated output follows current schema.org property names and structure for the selected type.

title: Schema Markup Validator for JSON-LD
description: Check JSON-LD structured data for schema.org compliance errors before it ships to production.
content: Structured data that is technically valid JSON can still be invalid schema markup, missing required properties, using the wrong type, or nesting objects incorrectly. This tool checks JSON-LD specifically against schema.org's requirements for the declared type, catching structural issues beyond basic JSON syntax.

faqs.question: Is this the same as checking for valid JSON syntax?
faqs.answer: No, this checks schema.org compliance specifically, required properties, correct types, and proper nesting, beyond just whether the JSON itself parses correctly.

faqs.question: Does a passing check guarantee rich results in Google?
faqs.answer: No, valid schema markup is a requirement for rich results eligibility, not a guarantee, since Google applies its own additional criteria and discretion.

title: Canonical Tag Checker, Spot Mismatched URLs
description: Check whether a page's canonical tag correctly matches its own URL or points elsewhere.
content: A canonical tag pointing to the wrong URL, an old version, a different domain, or a parameterized duplicate, can quietly tell search engines to ignore the page you actually want indexed. This tool checks a page's canonical tag against its own URL and flags whether they match or diverge.

faqs.question: What does it mean if the canonical tag doesn't match the page URL?
faqs.answer: It signals to search engines that a different URL should be treated as the primary version, which is sometimes intentional but often an unintended misconfiguration worth double checking.

faqs.question: Can I check a canonical tag from pasted HTML instead of a live URL?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can paste raw HTML directly if the page isn't publicly accessible yet.

title: Hreflang Tag Generator & Validator
description: Generate correct hreflang tags for multi-language pages and validate them for common return-tag errors.
content: Hreflang tags are notoriously error prone, a missing return tag on one language variant can invalidate the whole set. This tool generates correct hreflang tags for a set of language and region variants, and checks for the most common validation errors, like missing self-references and mismatched return tags.

faqs.question: What is a missing return tag error?
faqs.answer: Hreflang requires each page in a set to reference every other page, including itself. If page A points to page B but page B does not point back to page A, that is a return tag error.

faqs.question: Does this support region-specific language codes?
faqs.answer: Yes, both language-only codes like en, and region-specific codes like en-US or en-GB, are supported.

title: Redirect Chain Checker, See Every Hop
description: See every hop in a redirect chain and how many redirects a URL passes through before its final destination.
content: A URL that redirects through several hops before reaching its final destination wastes crawl budget and can dilute link value passed between pages. This tool follows a URL's full redirect chain and shows every hop, its status code, and the final destination, so you can spot and fix unnecessarily long chains.

faqs.question: How many redirect hops is too many?
faqs.answer: There is no strict cutoff, but each additional hop adds latency and complexity. A single redirect straight to the final destination is generally the cleanest approach where possible.

faqs.question: Does this catch redirect loops?
faqs.answer: Yes, a redirect loop, where a chain returns to a URL already visited, is detected and flagged rather than causing an endless check.

title: HTTP Header & Status Code Checker
description: Inspect a URL's full HTTP response headers and status code without opening dev tools.
content: Checking response headers for caching directives, security headers, or the exact status code a URL returns usually means opening browser dev tools or a terminal. This tool fetches and displays a URL's full HTTP response headers and status code directly, a quick way to check without leaving the browser tab.

faqs.question: What headers does this show?
faqs.answer: All standard HTTP response headers returned by the server, including status code, content type, caching directives, and security headers like Content-Security-Policy.

faqs.question: Can I check headers for a page that isn't live yet?
faqs.answer: No, this tool checks headers for a live, publicly accessible URL, since it performs a real HTTP request.

title: Broken Link Checker for a Single Page
description: Scan a page's links and flag which ones return a broken or error status.
content: A page with even a handful of broken outbound or internal links looks unmaintained to both visitors and search engines. This tool scans a single page's links and checks each one's response status, flagging broken or error results so you know exactly which links need fixing.

faqs.question: Does this check a whole site or just one page?
faqs.answer: This checks the links found on a single page you provide, rather than crawling an entire site.

faqs.question: What counts as a broken link?
faqs.answer: Any link returning a 4xx or 5xx status code, or failing to resolve at all, is flagged as broken.

title: Robots Meta Tag Generator (noindex, nofollow)
description: Build a correct robots meta tag with the exact index, follow, and archive directives you need.
content: A robots meta tag with the wrong combination of directives can accidentally deindex a page, or leave it indexed when it should not be. This tool builds a correct robots meta tag from a set of clear options, index or noindex, follow or nofollow, and additional directives like noarchive, avoiding syntax mistakes in a tag that is easy to get subtly wrong by hand.

faqs.question: What is the difference between noindex and nofollow?
faqs.answer: Noindex tells search engines not to include the page in results. Nofollow tells them not to pass ranking credit through the page's outbound links. They can be used independently or together.

faqs.question: Can I add multiple directives to one tag?
faqs.answer: Yes, directives like noindex, nofollow, and noarchive can be combined in a single robots meta tag as needed.

title: .htaccess Redirect Rule Generator
description: Generate correct .htaccess redirect rules without memorizing Apache rewrite syntax.
content: Apache's rewrite and redirect syntax in .htaccess is powerful but easy to get wrong, a single misplaced character can break an entire site's routing. This tool generates correct .htaccess redirect rules, single URL, wildcard, or domain-level redirects, from a simple form, without needing to write the raw syntax by hand.

faqs.question: Does this generate 301 or 302 redirects?
faqs.answer: Both are supported. 301 is used for permanent redirects, which pass SEO value to the destination, while 302 is used for temporary redirects.

faqs.question: Can I generate a wildcard redirect for an entire folder?
faqs.answer: Yes, wildcard and pattern-based redirect rules are supported alongside single URL redirects.

title: SEO-Friendly URL Slug Generator
description: Convert a page title into a clean, SEO-friendly URL slug, stripping stop words and special characters correctly.
content: A URL slug generated by simply lowercasing and hyphenating a title often ends up longer and messier than it needs to be. This tool converts a page title into a clean, SEO-friendly slug, stripping special characters, collapsing extra hyphens, and optionally removing common stop words, for a shorter, more readable URL.

faqs.question: Does this remove stop words like 'the' and 'and'?
faqs.answer: Yes, stop word removal is an optional setting, useful for keeping slugs shorter and more focused on the meaningful keywords.

faqs.question: How is this different from a general case converter?
faqs.answer: This is purpose-built for URL slugs specifically, handling special character stripping, stop words, and hyphenation together, rather than converting between programming naming conventions.

title: Keyword Density Checker for Any Text
description: See exact keyword and phrase frequency in a block of content, without needing to paste a live URL.
content: Checking how often a target keyword or phrase appears in a piece of content is a quick sanity check many writers still do manually. This tool analyzes pasted text and reports keyword and phrase frequency directly, no live URL or crawler required, useful for checking a draft before it is published.

faqs.question: Does this check single keywords or phrases too?
faqs.answer: Both, single word frequency and multi-word phrase frequency are reported separately.

faqs.question: Is keyword density still a meaningful SEO metric?
faqs.answer: It is a much smaller ranking signal than it once was, but checking for natural, non-repetitive language and confirming target terms actually appear remains a reasonable quick sanity check.

title: Text-to-HTML Ratio Checker
description: Check the ratio of visible text to total HTML markup on a page, a signal some SEO audits still flag.
content: A page with a very low ratio of visible text to total HTML markup can signal a bloated, code-heavy page with thin actual content. This tool calculates that ratio directly from a URL or pasted HTML, giving a quick, specific number rather than a vague sense of whether a page feels heavy.

faqs.question: What is considered a healthy text-to-HTML ratio?
faqs.answer: There is no single official threshold, but a very low ratio can indicate a code-heavy page with comparatively thin visible content, worth a closer look rather than treated as a hard rule.

faqs.question: Can I check pasted HTML instead of a live URL?
faqs.answer: Yes, both a live URL and pasted raw HTML are supported.

title: Image Alt Text Auditor for Any Page
description: Scan a page and list every image missing alt text, or with empty or unhelpful alt attributes.
content: Missing or unhelpful alt text affects both accessibility and image SEO, and it is easy for a few images to slip through unnoticed on a large page. This tool scans a page's images and lists which ones are missing alt text entirely, or have empty or clearly placeholder alt attributes, so they can be fixed in one pass.

faqs.question: Does this check for accessibility, SEO, or both?
faqs.answer: Both, missing or poor alt text is a genuine issue for screen reader accessibility and can also affect how search engines understand image content.

faqs.question: What counts as an unhelpful alt attribute?
faqs.answer: Empty alt attributes, generic placeholder text like 'image' or the filename itself, and alt text that clearly does not describe the image are flagged.

title: Meta Tag Extractor, See Every Tag on Any Page
description: Pull every meta tag from a page's head section into one readable list.
content: Manually scrolling through a page's raw HTML to check its meta tags is slow, especially when comparing your own page against a competitor's. This tool extracts every meta tag from a page's head section, title, description, canonical, Open Graph, robots directives, and more, into one clean, readable list.

faqs.question: Does this show Open Graph and Twitter card tags too?
faqs.answer: Yes, all meta tags found in the head section are listed, including standard SEO tags, Open Graph, and Twitter card tags.

faqs.question: Can I extract meta tags from a competitor's page?
faqs.answer: Yes, this works on any publicly accessible URL, useful for quick competitive checks alongside auditing your own pages.
